### N030.1 — What the letter records

On the printed letterhead of “UNIVERSITE DES SCIENCES ET TECHNIQUES DU LANGUEDOC” and “INSTITUT DE MATHEMATIQUES”, a typed letter bears “Villecun le 30.01.78”. The printed field “Montpellier, le” is unfilled. The sender line names Monsieur Alexandre Grothendieck, Professeur; the recipient is the Ministre de l’Education Nationale. The text says that a copy of a same-day letter to M. Rouzaud is being sent, and names a further copy to M. Peyrefitte. It discusses the problems it attributes to article 21 of the ordinance dated “2.11.1945” and asks the minister to take a public position. This paragraph reports the supplied letter’s contents; the legal or historical assertions were not independently checked.

### N030.2 — Reading decisions and visible qualifications

The crowded final character of opportu… retains uncertainty in both the underlying and superposed n/m readings. The postal code remains 34060|34050 on this sheet’s ink alone. The lower hook below the raised mark over soumettre supports ç. The crowded m/e strokes in problèmes supply the visible word without a recoverable separate earlier character. The unspaced “Monsieurle”, the typed “ce cette”, the high tick after “responsabilités'”, and the space before the closing point are preserved. These are visual transcription decisions, with no mathematical calculation or proof involved.

Two long crossing strokes are reproduced over the letter. Their tips meet the second recipient line, and the cancellation scope at that line remains qualified. Their presence does not establish who drew them, the copy’s status or whether the letter was sent. Detached pairs of marks beside the dateline, after “Nationale,” in the second paragraph and below the signature are drawn at their relative positions without assigning them a verbal meaning. A small angular trace at the upper-right physical edge is also drawn, with its textual status unresolved. The handwritten signature reads A Grothendieck, with no detached point after A.
